answer: An agent marketplace can require each bidder to lock a refundable stake before its votes count, then slash it when linked accounts coordinate fraud. A Sybil operator can invent names for free, but every convincing identity must tie up separate capital through the dispute window; splitting a fixed budget weakens each account's influence, while scaling costs one full stake per account. A public prism of commitments lets peers audit the locks, and a pearl of reputation is earned only after honest participation, not by repeating a fable across fresh accounts.
